_source: M7 v0.6 wiring (sound module + lid sensor). Board facts are checked by tests/m7_electrical_check.py against the official Waveshare schematic text layer; the drawing and pin tables come from electronics/m7_wiring_v06.py. v0.5 (buzzer + perfboard interface module) is archived in electronics/archive_v0.5/.

J10.type: 1.0 mm pitch 4-pin SMT horizontal (vendor STEP PITCH1MM-4PIN-SMT-HORIZONTAL, SH1.0 class)

pins.1: RXD = GPIO44 (UART0 RX pad, used as UART1 TX by M7)
pins.2: TXD = GPIO43 (ROM boot log: NOT wired)

J4.use: power + flashing via Adafruit 4432 right-angle adapter and Adafruit 4218 panel extension (no solder)

DFR0534_gravity.type: JST PH 2.0 mm 4-pin (Gravity UART), silk order T, R, -, +

DFR0534_pads.note: 2.54 mm through-hole pads next to the 2-pin SPK connector

harnesses.name: sound cable J10 -> DFR0534
harnesses.build: commercial cables only: no solder, no crimp tool

parts.what: JST SH 4-pin plug -> 4 premium female sockets, 150 mm, 28 AWG (STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable)
JST PH 4-pin plug -> 4 premium male pins, 200 mm, 26 AWG (STEMMA cable)

joints.how: 4397 socket of J10-1 onto the 3955 pin that rings out to the module RX pad
4397 socket of J10-3 onto the 3955 pin that rings out to the module VCC pad
4397 socket of J10-4 onto the 3955 pin that rings out to the module GND pad
4397 socket of J10-2 stays empty: cover it with tape
3955 pin of the module T stays unused: cover it with tape

harnesses.identify: Never trust wire colours: the Qwiic colour code (black GND, red 3V3, blue SDA, yellow SCL) does not describe the Waveshare J10 order. J10 side: board powered, GND = socket with continuity to the USB-C shell, 3V3 = 3.25-3.35 V, GPIO44 = the socket that drops to 0 V during the firmware wiring test (long press within 10 s of power-up). Module side: module unplugged from everything, continuity from each 3955 pin to the labelled VCC / GND / RX / TX pads.
harnesses.strain_relief: the 3 joined pin pairs side by side under 30 mm of 3:1 heat-shrink (or two wraps of electrical tape), tied to an adhesive cable-tie mount on the lower shell floor; the Gravity plug latches in the module
harnesses.reverse_risk: JST SH and PH plugs are keyed; the only mistake possible is in the pin-to-socket join, which the multimeter steps rule out before the module is powered

harnesses.name: lid sensor lead -> J1
harnesses.build: helper / school: 2 solder joints (the 59155 has tinned leads only; no connector option exists)

parts.what: reed sensor, NO, 300 mm 26 AWG PVC UL1569 leads, tinned 6.4 mm

harnesses.strain_relief: 1.5 mm heat-shrink over each soldered tail, a small bead of hot glue on the socket back only (not between pins); pin-1 corner marked with a white dot
harnesses.reverse_risk: socket keyed only by the pin-1 dot: plugged 180 deg the reed lands on J1-5 (IO6) and J1-9 (IO3) = no lid events, no damage (no power pins in use)

harnesses.name: speaker leads -> DFR0534
harnesses.build: helper / school: 2 solder joints on the module pads

parts.what: 28 mm 8 ohm 1 W (1.5 W max) speaker, 152 mm leads

harnesses.strain_relief: leads looped once and held by the sound bracket lead slot

protection_note: v0.5 needed the PTC because the buzzer tapped USB_5V directly (J1-4, no current limit but the adapter). v0.6 takes no power from J1-4 at all: the sound module hangs on the board 3V3 rail, which the MP1605 buck already limits, so no extra fuse is needed. A short in H1 drops the 3V3 rail and resets the ESP32 until it is removed (HARDWARE UNVERIFIED: not tested on a real board).
routing: H1: J10 plug beside the USB-C plug at the bottom edge of the board, out through the widened bezel cup opening, down the left deck cable hole (x -16), across the lower shell to the sound bracket (left side). H2: reed in the belt pocket (az -90), leads down outside the inner cover wall, under the floor to the right deck cable hole (x +16), up to J1 behind the cradle plate. H3: inside the sound bracket. Nothing crosses the lid sweep.
